title: Twisted Fate: Cowboys vs. Aliens - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K9Asd1xasRc

Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews *Twisted Fate: Cowboys vs. Aliens*, sent by Plaay Games after his History Maker Golf review. The box calls it "a story game of unlikely encounters", but Daniel says it's really a thematic dice game. You lead a posse of up to four cowboys defending their town from three aliens in turn.

There are three ways to lose: the alien reaches your town, it heals past the top of its health track, or it kills every active cowboy. There are also three ways to win each fight: deplete its health, drive it back off the cliff edge, or stack enough of one condition (dazed, restrained, wounded, distracted) to earn a kill shot. Each turn the alien rolls blue dice for an attack whose smash, surprise and fear effects are blocked by strong, smart and courageous cowboys. Cowards take double damage. You then assign white dice to your cowboys' attacks, where any 1 or 2 is a hit, and a miss hands the alien a counterattack. In his demo, a revolver applies a wound and Flint Eastwood's finisher then lands five damage. Rotating hurt cowboys into the reserve to heal adds another layer.

He found more decisions than the rules suggest, but wished it had reference cards and thinks it's overpriced at around $40, recommending it at $25–30. He also argues that the cut "desperation" deck, a last-gasp heroic reprieve the publisher sent him anyway, should go back in the box.

----

Should a game include a "heroic last stand" mechanic that can rescue a lost game, or does that cheapen the defeat?
